why: The paper names three artifacts (code/fraud_pipeline.py, code/multi_dataset_study.py, code/results_nested_cv/per_fold_metrics.csv) but gives no repository URL, no DOI-linked archive, and the repository inspection found nothing cloned. Nothing executable was released, so the Study A nested-CV pipeline (scaler + RF + inner 80/20 split + fold-averaged F1) has to be rebuilt from the protocol description in §3 and the config_for_value fields. The pipeline itself is ordinary scikit-learn work, so the rebuild is small; the only external dependency is the Kaggle creditcard.csv, which is publicly documented but requires a Kaggle account/API token or an equivalent mirror.
missing_artifacts: code/fraud_pipeline.py (Study A entrypoint; named in the Reproducibility section, no URL)
code/results_nested_cv/per_fold_metrics.csv (85 rows; filename truncated in the PDF)
creditcard.csv from Kaggle 'mlg-ulb/creditcardfraud' (not bundled; needs Kaggle credentials or a public mirror)
blockers_seen: no repository URL anywhere in the provided material; code_links are bare file paths with truncated filenames
Kaggle dataset download requires authentication (kaggle.json / API token); a mirror or manual download is needed
no GPU on this machine, but the paper states CPU-only and sklearn RandomForest cannot use one anyway

hyperparameters are only partially specified (n_estimators=100, max_depth=16 are given; random_state, min_samples_*, bootstrap defaults are not), so a rebuild must fix seeds and leave sklearn defaults otherwise

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: About 10-15 minutes of command time: ~2 min install (scikit-learn, imbalanced-learn, pandas, numpy, scipy), ~3-6 min to obtain and load the 144 MB creditcard.csv, ~3-5 min for the 5 outer-fold Random Forest fits (100 trees, max_depth 16, 227k x 30 rows each) with the inner 80/20 split, seconds for the fold-averaged F1. The paired threshold-tuning contrast (C2) adds ~1 min. The full Study B (2,025 fits on small datasets) would add ~8-12 min if time allowed.

compute.basis: 5 outer folds x (one inner 80/20 split + one Random Forest of 100 trees, max_depth 16 on ~227k x 30 float features) — roughly 20-40 s per fit on 8 CPU cores — plus a 2-6 min download and load of the 144 MB Kaggle CSV, all CPU-bound scikit-learn with no GPU path; the authors' own claim is ~9 min for the entire 85-fit Study A.
